summary.text: Julia Letlow is the U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District, elected in a March 2021 special election after the death of her husband, Luke Letlow, who had won the seat but died of complications of COVID-19 before taking office. Before Congress she worked as a university communications administrator and educator. She is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate, endorsed by President Trump, and her House website and campaign materials emphasize her work on law enforcement, workforce development, infrastructure funding and parental rights in education.

paragraphs.text: Born March 16, 1981, in Monroe, Louisiana, as Julia Barnhill; she graduated from Ouachita Christian High School.

Earned a Bachelor of Arts and Master of Arts in speech communication from the University of Louisiana at Monroe (ULM), and a doctorate in communication from the University of South Florida (Wikipedia gives 2012).

Worked at the Tulane University School of Medicine in New Orleans as director of education, director of resident patient safety and quality improvement, and a clinical instructor of anesthesiology; she also served as an instructor and teaching associate at ULM, Tulane and the University of South Florida.

Returned to ULM as ombudsperson and special projects coordinator for the Provost, then served as director of marketing and communications and, from 2018 to 2019, executive director of external affairs and strategic communications.

Her husband, Luke Letlow, won the 2020 election for the 5th District seat but died of COVID-19 complications days before taking office. She won the March 20, 2021 special election with 65 percent of the vote (her House biography) and took office in April 2021; she is the first Republican woman elected to Congress from Louisiana.
Re-elected outright in 2022 (67% of the vote) and 2024 (62.9%).

Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the subcommittees on Agriculture; Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education; and National Security and the Department of State, and on the Committee on Education and the Workforce.
Authored the Parents Bill of Rights (H.R. 5), which passed the House on March 24, 2023.

Announced her U.S. Senate candidacy on January 20, 2026. She finished first in the May 16 Republican primary, defeating incumbent Sen. Bill Cassidy, and won the June 27 runoff against state Treasurer John Fleming.
According to her House biography, she is the mother of two children.
